exposure: Rooming-in practice (consistent use vs. referral to nursery)
outcome: Mothers' perception and satisfaction with information received about rooming-in
cohort: Sixty-five healthy Italian women (average age=33.8 years old) who gave birth in a hospital offering 24h rooming-in.
finding: Women's degree of rooming-in application use differs based on the type of delivery and subsequent maternal physical condition, with those who had undergone Caesarean section more likely to use nursery care.
mod_finding: Women who had undergone Caesarean section were more likely to make use of the nursery care up to 72 hours after delivery.
cross-section timing: During hospitalization, from the moment of birth through to discharge, with observations on nursery use up to 72 hours after delivery.
